steps.message: A plain git clean -fdx would remove bin/ and obj/ along with everything else that isn't tracked by git -- and since binlogs are almost always gitignored too, that would take the performance-comparison history out along with the cruft. The fix is to exclude the binlogs explicitly rather than clean everything and try to restore them afterward.

Run git clean -fdx -e "*.binlog" (or the equivalent git clean -fdx --exclude=*.binlog). The -e/--exclude flag tells git clean to skip anything matching that pattern, so bin/, obj/, and other stray build output get removed while every *.binlog file in the tree is left untouched. I wouldn't reach for moving the binlogs to a separate folder first -- excluding them in place is simpler and avoids an extra step that could itself be forgotten.
